script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: friendship

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

EXT. SUBURBAN HOME - DAY

A warm summer breeze rustles the leaves. A beautiful, quaint suburban home sits proudly on its manicured lawn. The sun casts dappled shadows across the garden.

INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY

SARAH (30s, kind, loving, and motherly) sits on a worn, plush armchair, sewing a button onto her husband's favorite shirt.

JASON (30s, friendly, adventurous, and Sarah's husband), enters the room with a puzzled expression.

JASON
(quizzically)
What's this, dear?

SARAH
(smiling)
Just making sure your favorite shirt is in good condition for tomorrow's event.

JASON
(gratefully)
I knew I married the best woman in the world.

INT. KITCHEN - DAY

Jason and Sarah share a light-hearted banter while preparing dinner.

JASON
(playfully)
You know, dear, I've always wondered...

SARAH
(interrupting with a laugh)
What, my secret recipe for the perfect spaghetti sauce?

JASON
(teasingly)
Yes, that! But I also want to know how you manage to keep our lives so harmonious.

SARAH
(pausing to consider)
Well, it all starts with friendship. When you and I became friends, we built a solid foundation for our marriage.

INT. GARAGE - DAY

Jason tinkers with a vintage motorcycle as Sarah enters, holding a tray of sandwiches and a thermos of coffee.

SARAH
(loving)
Here you go, my dear. A little something to keep you fueled up while you work on your pride and joy.

JASON
(gratefully)
You're the best, Sarah. I'd be lost without you.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

The sun sets, casting a warm glow over the living room as Sarah reads aloud to Jason from a classic novel.

SARAH
(reading)
"Friendship is the hardest thing in the world to explain. It's not something you learn in school. But if you haven't learned the meaning of friendship, you really haven't learned anything."

Jason listens intently, looking deeply into Sarah's eyes.

JASON
(softly)
You're right. And I'm grateful every day that I have you as my friend and my partner.

INT. BACKYARD - DAY

Sarah and Jason sit under a tree, enjoying a quiet moment together. They laugh and share memories, their friendship shining through in every word and gesture.

SARAH
(looking at Jason lovingly)
You know, our bond is unbreakable. It's like the roots of this tree. No matter what life throws our way, our friendship will remain strong.

JASON
(smiling)
Absolutely, my love. Together, we can face any challenge and emerge even stronger.

INT. DINING ROOM - NIGHT

Sarah and Jason, along with their two teenage children, share a delicious dinner. They talk, laugh, and reminisce about old memories, creating new ones in the process.

As the night grows late, Sarah looks around the table, her heart swelling with gratitude.

SARAH
(tearfully)
You know, I am so grateful for this beautiful family, and for the deep, unbreakable bond we share. It's a true gift, and I'll cherish it forever.

FADE OUT.

THE END
